title: Grade 7 Math — Tue, Jun 17
description: Algebraic Expressions — Day 2 of 5: Like and unlike terms; addition
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Which pair are LIKE terms?
questions.explanation: Like terms have the same variable(s) raised to the same power(s). 4ab and 7ab both have ab, so they are like terms.

questions.question: Which pair are UNLIKE terms?
questions.explanation: Unlike terms have different variables or different powers. 5x and 3y have different variables (x vs y), making them unlike terms.

questions.question: Add: 3x + 5x
questions.explanation: 3x + 5x = (3 + 5)x = 8x. Only the coefficients are added; the variable x stays the same.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be simplified further?
questions.explanation: 6a + 3b has unlike terms (a and b), so it cannot be combined further. The other options all have like terms.

questions.question: What is the sum of 4a²b and 3a²b?
questions.explanation: 4a²b + 3a²b = (4 + 3)a²b = 7a²b. Like terms — same variable part a²b.

questions.question: Which terms in 4x² + 3x − 2x² + 5 are like terms?
questions.explanation: 4x² and −2x² both have x², so they are like terms and can be combined: 4x² − 2x² = 2x².

questions.question: Are 6abc and 6bca like terms?
options: No, because the letters are in different order
Yes, but only if a = b = c
questions.explanation: abc = bca = cab (multiplication is commutative). So 6abc and 6bca are like terms — both equal 6abc.
